jobs.title: Watchtower cache
jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: Civilization V Resource Outposts improvement portrait, reusable as its strategic-view emblem and management UI identity.
Input image 1 is the ACTUAL shipped Civ V Fort strategic-view icon, STYLE REFERENCE ONLY. Input image 2 is the ACTUAL shipped Civ V Trading Post strategic-view icon, STYLE REFERENCE ONLY. Make ORIGINAL subject artwork; do not copy either native subject.
Match these reference icons closely: small pale ivory and grey-green dimensional architectural pictograms with precise angular silhouettes, broad smooth lit faces and desaturated cool teal shaded sides. Almost sculpted ivory relief, strong three-quarter perspective, economical thin architectural members with clear gaps. Limited palette, quiet surface treatment, no realistic materials or brush texture. The structure should read at a 45-pixel icon size.
Compose ONE isolated icon: a very dark navy-black circular disk with a restrained glossy grey upper-half reflection, like the supplied references. The original pale structure sits centered on the disk. No metal ring or gold border. Icon circle occupies about 86% of a square canvas. Outside the circle is truly transparent. No letters, symbols resembling letters, labels, caption, watermark, or second icon.
This is a resource-claiming fortified outpost, independent of roads or trade routes. Keep the design era-neutral: no radar, antenna, guns, modern machinery, religious motifs, flags, road, caravan, city skyline, resource-specific tools, or particular resource type. A single LARGE plain banded storage crate is the generic resource motif.
Avoid miniature diorama landscapes, rocks, foliage, brick lines, fine scratches, small props, chunky toy rendering, photorealism, flat vector outlines and decorative rim. The reference defines the simplicity and material.
Subject option A — Watchtower cache: one slender open watch platform on four posts at the rear left, topped by a simple shallow pyramidal roof; a low L-shaped palisade of only five or six broad pale panels wraps its base on two sides. One large plain banded crate at front right, about one third of total pictogram width. Make three dominant masses: slim tower, low enclosure, large crate. The open tower must be clearly different from the stock solid stone Fort. No ladder rungs or timber grain, no pointed stakes repeated into visual noise. Small garrison space implied by a clear dark opening beside the crate. The structure occupies most of the circle but stays fully inside it.

Give the structure an uneven stepped silhouette and a small dark open garrison yard; avoid making a symmetrical castle. Keep the structure wholly within the circle.

jobs.title: Watchtower cache
jobs.prompt:
Use case: background-extraction.
Asset type: Civilization V worker construction action glyph for the Resource Outpost.
Input 1 is the EDIT TARGET, our original watchtower cache emblem. Input 2 is the actual native Civ V UnitActions atlas, a STYLE REFERENCE ONLY, never copy its subjects.
Extract ONLY the pale outpost structure and its one cargo crate from input 1, keeping the design, silhouette, relative proportions, orientation, roof profile, open gaps, and pale ivory/cool grey-green lighting. Remove the entire dark circular medallion and its gloss. ALL background must be genuinely transparent, including every gap between posts, the interior opening, and space around the crate. No disk, rim, base plate, badge, landscape, glow, external shadow, frame, text or watermark.
The resulting isolated pictogram must fit the native atlas: compact, economical smooth shaded planes, crisp edges, pale cream lit faces and subtle cool teal shaded sides. The fort and trading-post action glyphs in input 2 show the correct unframed treatment. Keep the architectural structure matching input 1, do not replace it with stock Fort art or add a hammer. Keep small incidental seams understated. Center one single glyph on a transparent square canvas, occupying 80 percent of the width or height, whichever is greater. One glyph only. This is a precise background removal and presentation adaptation, not a redesign.
